q3aaa4bf0.question: The lifecycle table has no way back from changes-requested for an unchanged artifact, so an artifact the reviewers did not object to must still change before it can rejoin a changes-requested request; should the common artifact model allow open-signoff also from changes-requested at an unchanged approved revision? The table belongs to the common artifact model, not to this Story, so it is not designed here.
q3aaa4bf0.rationale: Decided by the user: handle the model change now, in s8, to avoid extra work later. Add a lifecycle step so open-signoff is also allowed from changes-requested when the artifact's approval and other-party review are still of its current revision (unchanged content); prerequisiteFailure and openSignoff accept such a head; the revise-together rule then no longer applies, because an artifact nobody objected to rejoins the request unchanged. Includes the lifecycle.ts table change, its tests, and the changes to the s8 tests that assumed an unchanged changes-requested artifact is refused.

q1ee1d286.question: Re-running define on an existing Epic is not a claim unit, so a DEF in signoff is not gated against changes by non-holders; should define on an existing Epic be gated, and if so with which unit?
q1ee1d286.rationale: Decided by the user: define on an existing Epic stays ungated for now; recorded in docs/plans/team-workflow.md as a deferred item so it is not forgotten.

summary.prose: When reviewers ask for changes, the claim holder revises the artifacts of that request, reviews and approves each again locally, and submits them again; the submission goes to the same pull request, so the reviewers keep one thread, and the new signoff covers only the revisions that were pushed. Because a request with changes requested sends all of its artifacts back together, every artifact that is to stay in it must be revised before it can be resubmitted. A request for changes made on an earlier push is not mistaken for one on the new push, and re-authoring an artifact keeps its Signoff history so the earlier request can be found; an identical re-author of an artifact in signoff changes nothing. Re-authoring an artifact that is in signoff (the design.epic and design.story runs) is allowed only for the holder, and a unit nobody holds must be claimed first; other writers of the same artifacts are not gated here. It builds on the s7 submission and adds two optional tracker additions and a careful rule in the content write; no lifecycle or record type changes.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: A daemon-side team gate over a synchronous, capability-declaring tracker port (alternative a1). The port (sc1) is the only way the workflow library talks to a tracker; GitHub is its first adapter, made by extracting the existing GitHub code (src/workflow/tracker, the issue calls in tracker-auto.ts, and the create and close calls in src/workflow/bugfix/tracker.ts) behind it. sc1 is the one tracker abstraction: the unbuilt tracker-tool design (LLD-38436e90625a83a2-s1) is not built as a second abstraction and is superseded or amended by s1's LLD. The policy (sc2) is read from the remote default branch and says which stages need signoff, whether claims are enforced, the claim units and the administrators. The artifact's tracker record keeps every existing meta.tracker field exactly as it is and gains additive per-unit data, plus an optional meta.revision (sc3). The team gate (sc4) takes a guarded action and returns an outcome. Signoff is a separate record (sc5) that never changes meta.review or approvedAt. Syncing tracker status on git pull and push, and the issue-status read it needs, are deferred with the later-tracker work to a define extend and are not part of this HLD.

consumedContracts.name: Per-unit tracker record and revision
consumedContracts.purpose: Adds data next to the artifact's existing meta.tracker without changing any existing field: a per-stage-unit issue map in a new key, and an optional meta.revision (default 0 when absent), minted on content writes and not on meta-only writes. A review that applies auto-fixes, whether through verdicts.ts or run-artifact.ts, is a content write; a report-only review is meta-only. Owned by s4, which also owns the inventory of artifact write paths and the shared issue-creation code.

consumedContracts.name: Team gate, claim state, gate outcome, refusal error and completion hook
consumedContracts.purpose: The single gate for guarded actions in the daemon-owned workflow library, the claim state read live from the tracker, the outcome type, the typed refusal error that leaves approval, the review-fix decision that both review paths (verdicts.ts and run-artifact.ts) consult, and a completion hook that s5 ships unregistered and s7 registers. The gate derives the acting user itself through the port, so no caller signature changes. Owned by s5; s4 supplies issue creation which the gate calls for the no-issue outcome.

consumedContracts.name: SignoffRecord
consumedContracts.purpose: A record separate from meta.review and approvedAt, stating that a signoff request completed and which artifacts and revisions it covered. The revision is the binding; a content hash is later hardening. Owned by s7.

boundary.internal: Revision of an open request: re-run of local approval, push to the same request, discarding an earlier completion, refusing non-holders.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The GitHub adapter built by extracting src/workflow/tracker (including the existing signed-in-user read, ghCurrentLogin, behind whoAmI), the issue calls in tracker-auto.ts and the create and close calls in src/workflow/bugfix/tracker.ts behind the port; the gh command wrapper with its 10-second timeout; contract tests; detection of a missing tool or sign-in. The port receives the needed capabilities as an argument, so s1 does not read the policy. Reconciliation: the unbuilt tracker-tool design LLD-38436e90625a83a2-s1 (docs/standalone/add-add-items-tracker-setting-have-E2026100638436e90/S001/LLD.md) is not built as a second abstraction; sc1 is the one tracker abstraction and s1's LLD supersedes or amends that LLD, once its conflicting approval status is settled. Syncing tracker status on git pull and push, and an issue-status read on the port, are deferred to the define extend.

Reading the policy file from the remote default branch ref, the cached last-fetched copy and the offline rule, finding the first default-branch commit that carried the policy file, the starter policy and the team setup command.

The repo-scoped kind of row in the shared settings catalog whose reads and writes go to the per-repo map in github.json read by resolveGithubConfig; its rendering in VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal client; read-only display of policy values. Shares the single store with s1's target resolution.

Shared issue-creation code refactored out of autoPushEpicOnHld, autoPushStoryOnLld and autoPushTasksOnPlan, find-by-label dedupe for Story and Task issues, forcing Task issues on in team mode, daemon-side triggering when a draft is first written, the terminal approve path kept as manual fallback, the inventory and classification of artifact write paths (including the two writeFileSync writers, and both verdicts.ts and run-artifact.ts as content writes when auto-fixes change the body), the single content-write helper and the revision minting, the bypass test that also detects raw writeFileSync on artifact paths, and the rule that an artifact without meta.revision reads as revision 0.

The team gate and its call sites (daemon step entry points and approveArtifactByJsonPath), the acting-user read through the port, claim and release commands, live assignee reads, the guarded-action list (code-review and analyze are never guarded; review is never refused), the report-only review for a non-holder through the review-fix decision on both review paths (verdicts.ts and run-artifact.ts), the typed TeamGateRefusedError, its handling beside ReviewBlockedError in approveWorkflowTarget and its formatting in the terminal client's approve case in src/cli/command.ts, the no-issue outcome handling, administrator release, and the declaration of the completion hook, shipped unregistered.
Parking a draft on a handoff branch, the issue note, resuming from committed files, and reconstructing in-flight workflow state from committed artifacts instead of the opaque token.

Opening the signoff request with the chosen artifacts, prerequisite checks for model review and local approval, registering the completion hook to produce the awaiting-signoff outcome, the on-demand completion check, automatic release of the claim on completion, recording sign-off together, grandfathering of artifacts approved before the policy anchor, and the separate display of signoff.
Private implementation of s9: Keep tracker issues and status in step with the work without a manual step

nonFunctional.performance: Each guarded action makes at most two live reads through the port (the signed-in user and the assignee); every tracker command has a 10-second timeout, after which the action is refused with the reason. A repo without a policy makes no tracker call.
nonFunctional.security: Policy is read only from the remote default branch ref and is not locally overridable; enforcement lives in the daemon-owned workflow library (k1); no tracker secrets are stored by insrc, sign-in stays with the tracker's CLI; administrators come only from the policy.
nonFunctional.observability: Every gate outcome other than allowed is logged with unit, action and reason; port failures carry their kind (missing-tool, missing-signin, unreachable, rejected).
nonFunctional.durability: Claim, issue and signoff state live in the tracker and in committed artifact files; the in-memory step state stores (100 entries, 1 hour) are not relied on for handoff. Artifact writes stay atomic through the existing helper.

api.name: openSignoff
api.signature: openSignoff(repo: string, unit: UnitRef, artifactIds: readonly string[], deps?: SignoffDeps): Promise<PortResult<SignoffRequestRef>>

parameters.name: unit
parameters.purpose: The Epic or Story unit that holds the artifacts.

parameters.name: artifactIds
parameters.purpose: The artifacts to submit; a revised artifact is submitted the same way as a first one.

returns.meaning: The request the artifacts are now recorded against: the earlier request when this was a revision of one that is still open, otherwise a new one.

errors.condition: Not the holder, nobody holds the issue, an artifact is not approved at its current revision (including one still in changes-requested because it was not revised) or its review is not of the current revision or not by the other party, the current branch is not the request's branch, or the chosen artifacts belong to different earlier requests.
The tracker could not be loaded or read (missing-tool, missing-signin, unreachable, rejected); a failed read of the earlier request never falls back to opening a new one.

preconditions: Team mode with signoff stages listed; the caller holds the unit's issue.
Each artifact is approved at its current revision with a review of that revision by the other party.
postconditions: The earlier request of an artifact is the one named by the LAST entry of signoffsOfMeta(meta) whatever its revision (signoffViewOf shows only the current revision, so it is not used for this).

When that entry is open or changes-requested and readSignoffRequest says the request is still open, the artifact files are pushed to the request's branch, no second request is created and every artifact is recorded open-signoff with the same Reference at its current revision.
When the earlier request is merged or closed, the tracker has no readSignoffRequest, or there is no earlier entry, a new request is opened as in s7.
An entry of an earlier revision is never edited, so an earlier completion cannot cover the new revision.

Every artifact of a request that had changes requested is in changes-requested and can rejoin only after a content change, a review and an approve; an artifact that was not revised is refused and may be left out of the submission, in which case it stays changes-requested under the old request.

api.name: prerequisiteFailure
api.signature: prerequisiteFailure(repo: string, unit: UnitRef, artifactId: string, stage: SignoffStage, meta: unknown, d: SignoffDeps): string | undefined

parameters.name: unit
parameters.purpose: The unit that holds the artifact.

parameters.name: meta
parameters.purpose: The head's stored meta, read through accessors.

returns.meaning: The reason the artifact cannot be submitted, or undefined when it can.

postconditions: For a DEF, HLD or LLD the review must exist, be by the other party and be of the head's current revision; before, only the first two were checked and the third was left to 'approve', which an override reason skips. A BUILD still uses the Story's code-review record.
A head in changes-requested is refused with its status named and a hint that it must be revised (content changed, reviewed and approved again) or left out of the submission.

api.name: readSignoffRequest
api.signature: readSignoffRequest?(ref: SignoffRequestRef): PortResult<{ branch: string; open: boolean }>

parameters.name: ref
parameters.purpose: The request whose head branch and openness are wanted.

returns.meaning: The branch the request was opened from and whether it can still take pushes (open, not merged and not closed).

errors.condition: gh missing, not signed in, unreachable, or the request not found (rejected).

postconditions: Reads only; nothing is changed in the tracker.

api.name: readSignoffState

parameters.name: since
parameters.purpose: ISO time the latest submission was recorded; a changes-requested decision counts only when made after it.

returns.meaning: completed when merged; changes-requested when closed unmerged, or when, among each reviewer's latest decisive review (APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED or DISMISSED; COMMENTED ignored), one requests changes and was submitted after `since`; otherwise open.

errors.condition: gh missing, not signed in, unreachable, malformed ref or unreadable output (rejected).

postconditions: With no `since` the answer is as in s7.
A lingering CHANGES_REQUESTED decision older than `since` does not make the request changes-requested, and a plain comment after it does not clear one made after `since`.

api.name: settleSignoff
api.signature: settleSignoff(repo: string, unit: UnitRef, deps?: SignoffDeps): Promise<readonly string[]>

parameters.name: unit
parameters.purpose: The unit whose open requests are read.

postconditions: For each open request it reads, it passes the `at` of the last Signoff entry of the waiting heads as `since`, so only a request for changes made after the latest submission is recorded.
As in s7, a request with changes requested moves every waiting head of the request to changes-requested together.

api.name: settleBeforeAuthor

parameters.name: intent
parameters.purpose: The authoring run: its workflow, repo and params.

returns.meaning: Returns when signoff no longer blocks the stage the run follows; otherwise throws.

errors.condition: blockedBySignoff still blocks the followed stage after settling its signoff.

preconditions: Awaited before assertMayAuthor at every authoring entry (src/daemon/steps/workflow-step/phases/start.ts, src/daemon/workflow-rpc.ts).
postconditions: Unchanged from s7: it settles the followed unit and refuses with the action 'author' and the workflow, whatever action assertMayAuthor later asks the gate. The upstream signoff block therefore still applies to a run that is a revise: a design.story run on an LLD whose HLD is no longer signed off is refused here before the gate is asked.

api.name: assertMayAuthor

parameters.name: intent
parameters.purpose: The authoring run: its workflow, repo and params.

returns.meaning: Returns when the run may change the stage; otherwise throws.

errors.condition: The gate refuses the action (held by another user), or the artifact the run would write is in signoff and nobody holds the unit.

preconditions: The run is a design.epic run (it writes the HLD) or a design.story run (it writes the LLD) on an existing unit.
postconditions: When the artifact the run would write is in-signoff or changes-requested the gate is asked with 'revise', and when the gate allows it the entry reads the holder itself (teamContext and readHolder, both exported by the gate) and refuses with a claim-first outcome if nobody holds the unit; no claim is taken. Otherwise the gate is asked with 'author' as before. 'revise' only changes the claim handling: the upstream signoff block is enforced earlier by settleBeforeAuthor.

Scope: this gates the authoring runs only. Other writers that change a DEF, HLD or LLD body with writeArtifact 'content' (resolveComment, appendStoryToDefine and any other caller outside the authoring runs) are not gated by this Story and are raised as an open question. A define run is not a claim unit (authorUnitOf gives it none), so DEF is not covered here; a plan run writes the PLAN, which is not a signoff stage.

api.name: writeArtifact
api.signature: writeArtifact(path: string, next: unknown, kind: WriteKind, opts?: { replaceUnreadable?: boolean }): number

parameters.name: next
parameters.purpose: The next head; an object with a meta object.

errors.condition: As today: next is not an object with a meta object.

postconditions: On a content write whose prior head has at least one entry in meta.lifecycle.signoffs and whose next head has no lifecycle or a lifecycle with no signoffs: when the content CHANGED, the stored lifecycle is the default draft with the prior Signoff entries carried and the revision minted as today (approval and review are not carried); when the content is UNCHANGED and the next head has NO lifecycle, the prior lifecycle is kept exactly as it is (status, approval, review, Signoff entries) and no draft lifecycle is synthesized, so no illegal transition is attempted and no error is thrown.
When the content is unchanged and the next head carries a lifecycle, behaviour is as today and is not changed here.
A prior head with no Signoff entry is written exactly as today.

api.name: signoffViewOf

returns.meaning: The Signoff entry at the head's current revision, or none.

postconditions: Unchanged: for a revised, re-approved head it shows no signoff until it is submitted again, and then shows the new entry; the earlier request is read from signoffsOfMeta, not from this view.

dataModelChanges.details: No field changes. A request may now be named by more than one Signoff entry of the same artifact, one per submitted revision, newest last; an entry's `at` is the time that submission was recorded. An entry is never edited after its request is recorded signed-off or changes-requested, and signed-off and signoff-changes move only the last entry when it is open (lifecycle.ts:255-262), so a completion of revision n cannot cover revision n+1. A content write now carries the entries forward instead of resetting them.

Today a content write stores the next head's lifecycle (or none), so a re-authored artifact in signoff loses its Signoff history (no meta.lifecycle, or signoffs reset to []), and an unchanged re-author with a freshly synthesized lifecycle would throw. The write now keeps the prior history in two cases only: changed content with no next lifecycle (or one with no signoffs) stores the default draft with the prior Signoff entries; unchanged content with no next lifecycle keeps the prior lifecycle as it is. Approval and review are never carried through a change: a changed artifact is a draft that needs both again.

Optional readSignoffRequest(ref) returning { branch, open }, and an optional `since` argument on readSignoffState. The GitHub adapter implements them with gh pr view --json headRefName,state and gh pr view --json state,mergedAt,reviews, and declares nothing new: the existing signoff-request capability covers both.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Relies on content writes minting a new meta.revision and returning the artifact to draft, so a revised artifact must be reviewed and approved again at the new revision before openSignoff accepts it; and needs the content write to keep the prior Signoff history (changed content) and the whole prior lifecycle (unchanged content, no next lifecycle), which is one amendment to sc3 proposed in the error paths (the helper belongs to s4). Other content writers outside the authoring runs are not changed here.

Calls the existing 'revise' guarded action from the authoring runs (design.epic and design.story) on an artifact in signoff, and reads the holder through the gate's exported teamContext and readHolder to refuse an unassigned unit; 'revise' never takes a claim. The hook returns 'continue' for 'revise' (signoff.ts:311-313), so the upstream block comes from settleBeforeAuthor, which refuses with 'author' before the gate is asked. No outcome or hook type changes and no amendment to sc4 is needed.
Records the new Signoff entry through the s7 open-signoff path; the SignoffRecord derived from heads groups entries by request and revision, so a resubmitted request shows its latest revision.

errorCases.scenario: A revised artifact is submitted without being reviewed and approved again
errorCases.detection: prerequisiteFailure finds the head is draft, or approved at an earlier revision than its current one, or without a review that exists, is by the other party and is of the current revision
errorCases.response: openSignoff returns a rejected result naming the artifact and what is missing; nothing is pushed
errorCases.userImpact: The holder is told to review and approve the revision first (ac36); an override-approved revision with a stale review is told to be reviewed again

errorCases.scenario: An artifact of a request that had changes requested is submitted without having been revised
errorCases.detection: prerequisiteFailure reads the head's lifecycle status as changes-requested (the status settleSignoff gave every waiting head of the request together) and refuses it, because open-signoff needs approved and the lifecycle table has no step out of changes-requested except a content change
errorCases.response: openSignoff returns a rejected result naming the artifact, its status changes-requested, and that it must be revised (content changed, reviewed and approved again) or left out of the submission; nothing is pushed or recorded for any artifact of the submission
errorCases.userImpact: The holder revises that artifact too, or resubmits without it; the stage it belongs to stays blocked until it is revised

errorCases.scenario: Someone who does not hold the claim re-authors an artifact that is in signoff through the design.epic or design.story run
errorCases.detection: assertMayAuthor finds the artifact in-signoff or changes-requested and asks the gate with 'revise'; the gate reads the assignee and it is another user
errorCases.response: TeamGateRefusedError with held-by-other and the holder; the authoring run does not start
errorCases.userImpact: The refusal names the holder (ac38, for the authoring runs)

errorCases.scenario: A user tries to re-author an artifact in signoff on a unit nobody holds
errorCases.detection: The gate allows 'revise' for an unassigned unit; assertMayAuthor then reads the holder through teamContext and readHolder and finds nobody
errorCases.response: TeamGateRefusedError with a refused outcome saying the unit must be claimed first; the claim is not taken
errorCases.userImpact: They claim the unit, then revise (ac38)

errorCases.scenario: A run re-authors an artifact in signoff while the stage it follows is no longer signed off
errorCases.detection: settleBeforeAuthor (awaited before assertMayAuthor at every authoring entry) calls settleForAttempt with 'author' and the workflow, and blockedBySignoff still blocks the followed stage, for example an HLD returned to draft or changes-requested after the LLD was submitted
errorCases.response: TeamGateRefusedError awaiting-signoff naming the request; the run does not reach assertMayAuthor, so the 'revise' choice cannot bypass the upstream block, which signoffCompletionHook does not check for 'revise'

errorCases.scenario: The earlier request cannot be read from the tracker (offline, not signed in, request not found)
errorCases.response: openSignoff returns that failure; it does not fall back to opening a new request, so the thread is never split by an outage
errorCases.userImpact: Submission is refused with the tracker's reason; retry when reachable

errorCases.detection: The branch publishBranch returns differs from the branch readSignoffRequest reports
errorCases.response: openSignoff returns a rejected result naming both branches; nothing is recorded

errorCases.scenario: The chosen artifacts name different earlier open requests
errorCases.detection: More than one distinct request Reference among the last Signoff entries (any revision) that are open or changes-requested
errorCases.response: Rejected, asking for separate submissions, as for in-signoff heads in s7

errorCases.scenario: The push to the request branch succeeds but recording an artifact fails
errorCases.response: The result names the artifact and the request; no new pull request exists. A repeat finds the earlier request again (still open) and records the rest
A resubmission is treated as a first submission: a new request is opened as in s7, and openSignoffRequest reuses an open pull request on the branch
errorCases.userImpact: No worse than s7; the thread may be split on such a tracker

errorCases.scenario: A changes-requested decision is stale: made on an earlier push
errorCases.detection: readSignoffState is given `since` (the last Signoff entry's `at`) and each reviewer's latest decisive review that requests changes was submitted at or before it

errorCases.userImpact: A resubmission is not cancelled by feedback on the old push

errorCases.scenario: A re-authored artifact in signoff loses its Signoff history

errorCases.scenario: An identical re-author of an artifact in signoff would be routed through an illegal transition to draft

errorCases.userImpact: Re-running a stage with identical output does not fail or move the artifact

edgeCases.input: The reviewer merges the request while the author's revision is still a local draft
edgeCases.expected: The head is not in-signoff so settle does not record it; the merged content is of an earlier revision and is not carried over. The artifact needs its own request at the new revision, and because the earlier request is merged a new one is opened

edgeCases.input: A resubmission whose earlier request was merged or closed
edgeCases.expected: readSignoffRequest reports not open, so a new request is opened; the old Signoff entry is left as it is

edgeCases.input: A reviewer who asked for changes on the old push approves the new push

edgeCases.input: A reviewer requests changes after the latest submission and then leaves a plain comment

edgeCases.expected: The decisive review is older than `since`, so the request is open and the resubmission stands

edgeCases.input: A request of two artifacts on which changes were requested, and the reviewers only objected to one of them

The holder revises the objected one and also has to change the other before it can be resubmitted; if it is left out, it stays changes-requested under the old request and its stage stays blocked until it is revised. edgeCases.expected: The content write behaves as today: nothing is carried and no lifecycle is created that the next head did not have

edgeCases.expected: Behaviour is as today and is not changed by this Story; the case is out of scope and unchanged

alternativesConsidered.name: Resubmit through openSignoff to the request the earlier Signoff entry names, with a stale-decision guard, a content write that keeps the Signoff history, revise-together for a changes-requested request, and a revise gate on the authoring runs
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A repeat submission of revised artifacts finds the request named by the last Signoff entry of their heads, pushes to that request's branch and records new open entries with the same Reference; a content write keeps the Signoff history; every artifact of a changes-requested request that stays in it must be revised and approved again; the authoring runs ask the gate with 'revise'; settle ignores a changes-requested decision older than the entry.
alternativesConsidered.approach: No new lifecycle operation: a content change already returns an artifact to draft at a new revision. The content write (writeArtifact, owned by s4 under sc3) keeps the prior head's lifecycle history the way it already keeps meta.tracker and meta.envelope, in two cases only. When the content CHANGED and the next head's lifecycle is missing or has none, the stored lifecycle is the default draft with the prior Signoff entries carried (approval and review are not carried). When the content is UNCHANGED and the next head has no lifecycle, the prior lifecycle is kept exactly as it is, so an identical re-author of an in-signoff or changes-requested head neither throws nor changes status. openSignoff then reads the LAST entry of signoffsOfMeta(meta) of each chosen head whatever its revision (signoffViewOf shows only the current revision). When that entry is open or changes-requested and the tracker's readSignoffRequest says the request is still open, the submission is a revision of that request: the files are committed and pushed to the request's branch (the current branch must be that branch) and open-signoff is recorded with the same Reference, which appends a new entry at the new revision. When the earlier request is merged or closed, or there is none, a new request is opened as in s7. When changes are requested, settleSignoff moves EVERY waiting head of the request to changes-requested together, and the lifecycle table has no step back from changes-requested except a content change, so every artifact that is to stay in that request must be revised (content changed), reviewed and approved again, and resubmitted with the others; an artifact re-authored with identical content stays changes-requested and prerequisiteFailure refuses it, naming that it must be revised or left out of the submission. An artifact left out stays changes-requested under the old request and its stage stays blocked until it is revised. prerequisiteFailure also requires the review's revision to equal the current revision. readSignoffState takes an optional `since` (the `at` of the last Signoff entry) and counts a changes-requested decision only when each reviewer's latest decisive review (APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED or DISMISSED; COMMENTED ignored) is a request for changes submitted after `since`; a closed unmerged request stays changes-requested. The authoring runs (design.epic for the HLD, design.story for the LLD) ask the gate with 'revise' when their artifact is in-signoff or changes-requested; the entry itself refuses when nobody holds the unit. The upstream signoff block is unchanged: the entries await settleBeforeAuthor first, which settles the followed stage and refuses with the action 'author' whatever action assertMayAuthor then asks. The gate covers the authoring runs only; other writers of the same artifacts (resolveComment, appendStoryToDefine) are not gated by this Story and are raised as an open question. A define run is not a claim unit and is not covered.
pros: Smallest change that meets ac36 to ac38 for the authoring runs: no lifecycle operation or record type change; reuses the s7 submission and the revision binding
One review thread: every Signoff entry of the request carries the same Reference, and a re-author keeps them
An identical re-author of an artifact in signoff is safe: it neither throws nor loses the lifecycle
The stale-decision guard stops a lingering CHANGES_REQUESTED from cancelling a good resubmission
A completed entry of an earlier revision cannot cover a later one
The meaning of a changes-requested request is explicit: its artifacts change together or not at all
The upstream signoff block holds for a revise because the entries settle with 'author' first
cons: Two additive amendments to contracts other stories own: sc1 (port read and `since`) and sc3 (content write keeps the Signoff history)
An artifact the reviewers did not object to still has to change before it can rejoin the request, because the lifecycle table has no way back from changes-requested
Other writers of the same artifacts are not gated, so a non-holder can still move an artifact in signoff to draft through them until a follow-up gates them
The author must be on the request's branch to resubmit; a mismatch is refused with the branch name
A reviewer's re-review of a new push is still needed on GitHub, so the guard can only avoid a false cancel, not force a re-review

alternativesConsidered.name: Keep the request reference outside the lifecycle
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Record the request a unit's artifacts were submitted under in the unit's tracker record, so a re-author cannot lose it, and read it from there on a resubmission.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Store the request Reference for each stage in meta.tracker.units (or a new key beside it), written by openSignoff, which a content write already carries forward (carryTracker). A resubmission reads the Reference from there instead of from the Signoff entries, and the Signoff entries are recorded as in s7. No change to the content write. The 'revise' gate, the `since` guard, the review-revision check and the port read are as in a1.
pros: No change to the content-write helper
The thread link survives a re-author through an existing carry
cons: Two places record the same fact (the Signoff entry and the tracker record), which can disagree
Changes the shape of meta.tracker, which sc3 keeps exactly as it is, so it needs a different amendment to sc3
A Signoff entry that names a request is still lost on a re-author, so the display and the next-stage block still read a reset history
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Records one fact twice, changes the shape of meta.tracker that sc3 keeps as it is, and still resets the Signoff entries that display and the next-stage block read (partial on ac37, sc3 and sc5).

alternativesConsidered.name: An explicit lifecycle revise step, a separate reviseSignoff function and a gate on every content writer
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add a lifecycle operation that takes changes-requested back to draft or approved, a separate reviseSignoff that pushes to the existing request, and gate every writeArtifact content caller with 'revise'.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add a 'revise' lifecycle operation (changes-requested back to draft) and a reviseSignoff(repo, unit, artifactIds) function next to openSignoff. It asks the gate with 'revise', requires each artifact approved at its current revision with a current review, pushes to the request's branch and records open-signoff against the same Reference. openSignoff refuses artifacts that already have an earlier request. This would also let an unchanged artifact rejoin without a content change. Every content writer of an artifact in signoff (the authoring runs, resolveComment, appendStoryToDefine and any other writeArtifact 'content' caller) would ask the gate with 'revise'. The history still has to survive a re-author, so the content write change is needed here too.
pros: Revision is a named step in the lifecycle and the history
A clean split between first submission and resubmission
An artifact no one objected to could rejoin the request unchanged
No writer could move an artifact in signoff to draft without the holder
cons: Changes the lifecycle table of the common artifact model, which this Story does not own
Touches write paths owned by other stories and by the s4 inventory
Duplicates most of openSignoff; a content write already returns the artifact to draft
A second entry point for a user to choose between
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Would close every content writer and let an unchanged artifact rejoin, but changes the lifecycle table that this Story does not own (partial on k3 and sc3), touches write paths owned elsewhere and adds a second entry point; it still needs the content-write change. Its two advantages are kept as open questions.

alternativesConsidered.name: Open a new request and close the old one
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A revision opens a fresh signoff request and closes the earlier one with a pointer to it.
alternativesConsidered.approach: openSignoff always opens a new request; when an earlier request exists for an artifact in changes-requested, the tracker closes it with a comment linking to the new one. No branch read, stale-decision guard or Signoff history is needed because each request is its own pull request.
pros: No branch matching, no stale-decision problem and no history to carry
Each pull request is a clean diff of one revision
cons: Breaks ac37: the reviewers' thread is lost, so it is no longer the single review thread
A reviewer who approves the old pull request after the author moved on completes a request nothing records
Needs a close-request operation on the port, another amendment
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: A new request per revision loses the single review thread ac37 requires and strands an approval on the old pull request.

openQuestions: Re-running define on an existing Epic is not a claim unit, so a DEF in signoff is not gated against changes by non-holders; should define on an existing Epic be gated, and if so with which unit?

The lifecycle table has no way back from changes-requested for an unchanged artifact, so an artifact the reviewers did not object to must still change before it can rejoin a changes-requested request; should the common artifact model allow open-signoff also from changes-requested at an unchanged approved revision? The table belongs to the common artifact model, not to this Story, so it is not designed here.

Writers other than the authoring runs also change a DEF, HLD or LLD body without a team gate: resolveComment (src/workflow/resolve-comment.ts:248-251, reached from the workflow.resolveComment handler at src/daemon/index.ts:739-745) and appendStoryToDefine (src/workflow/gates.ts:209-220). A content change returns the artifact to draft, so a non-holder can move an artifact in signoff to draft through them. Should every content writer of an artifact in signoff or changes-requested ask the gate with 'revise'? This Story gates the authoring runs only; gating the other writers is deferred to a follow-up.
